## The Core Systems Tension: High-Capacity Learned Models vs. Deterministic Real-Time Control

A physical AI machine is not a single, monolithic neural network running on a cloud server. It is an integrated physiological system comprising five distinct sensory-motor organs operating across different temporal rates, silicon fabrics, and trust boundaries.

```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        THE 5 ORGANS OF THE AGENT ARCHITECTURE                          │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                                        │
│  [PHOTONS] ──► 1. PERCEPTION (Chapter 4)                                               │
│                     │ (Spatial Affordance Tokens)                                      │
│                     ▼                                                                  │
│                2. MEMORY (Chapter 5) ◄── (SE(3) Frame Trees & Latent Belief)           │
│                     │                                                                  │
│                     ▼                                                                  │
│                3. REASONING (Chapter 6: System 2 · 1 Hz VLM Expiring Leases)           │
│                     │                                                                  │
│                     ▼                                                                  │
│                4. PLANNING (Chapter 7: System 1.5 · 20–50 Hz ACT Action Chunks)        │
│                     │                                                                  │
│   ══════════════════╪════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════  │
│   THE PRIVILEGE GATE: Proposal Verification & Control Barrier Functions (CBF)          │
│   ══════════════════╪════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════  │
│                     ▼                                                                  │
│                5. REFLEX (Chapter 8: System 1 · 1 kHz Bare-Metal MCU Enforcer)         │
│                     │                                                                  │
│                     ▼                                                                  │
│              [MOTOR INVERTERS / PHYSICAL WORLD]                                        │
│                     │                                                                  │
│                     ▼ (Endogenous Physical Mutation W_t ──► W_t+1)                     │
│              [NEW PHOTONS / SENSOR DRIFT] ──► [PERCEPTION (Ch 4)]                      │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The fundamental systems challenge of embodied intelligence is the **Privilege and Temporal Mismatch**:
* **The Cognitive Layer (Perception, Memory, Reasoning, Planning):** High-capacity deep learning models (ViTs, JEPAs, VLMs, Diffusion Policies) excel at unstructured perception, long-horizon task reasoning, and multi-step trajectory generation. But they are computationally heavy, require hundreds of milliseconds, experience memory bus contention, and produce stochastic outputs with long tail distributions ($P_{99}$).
* **The Physical Layer (Reflex & Motor Control):** Physical mechanics, inertial momentum ($p=mv$), and gearbox gears require strict, deterministic, microsecond-accurate current loops ($1000\text{ Hz}$) with smooth derivative continuity ($\mathcal{C}^2$) and non-negotiable mathematical guarantees that safety invariants are never violated.

Part II resolves this tension by systematically constructing, isolating, and validating each of the five sensory-motor organs across the Proposal–Permission boundary.

---

## The Five Sensory-Motor Organs of Part II

### 1. Perception (Chapter 4)
Ingesting high-bandwidth raw sensor streams without starving shared memory buses. We measure the pre-inference DMA bus tax during multi-camera streaming, eliminate cache thrashing through zero-copy ring buffers, and deploy Vision Transformers (ViTs) and self-supervised models (DINOv2) to extract compact **3D spatial affordance tokens** (`OBS-01`).

### 2. Memory (Chapter 5)
Bridging discrete, asynchronous sensor arrivals with continuous temporal belief. We maintain dynamic $SE(3)$ spatial frame graphs, deploy latent predictive world models (JEPAs / RSSMs) that anticipate future states in representation space without rendering heavy pixels, and enforce **State Validity TTL Leases** to revoke authority when sensory tracking is occluded (`STATE-01`).

### 3. Reasoning (Chapter 6)
Harnessing foundation Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for open-world semantic goal grounding without ceding direct actuator authority. We translate natural language commands into 3D metric bounding boxes, filter proposals through non-blocking kinematic reachability bounds ($\kappa(J)$), and emit time-bounded **Expiring Intent Leases** ($t_{\text{expire}}$) (`INTENT-01`).

### 4. Planning (Chapter 7)
Decoding high-level semantic intent into continuous, multi-step joint trajectories at $20\text{--}50\text{ Hz}$. We deploy modern Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) and diffusion policies predicting $H$-step future waypoint horizons in parallel, applying temporal ensembling and spline interpolation to guarantee $\mathcal{C}^2$ jerk continuity and prevent gearbox gear wear (`PLAN-01`).

### 5. Reflex (Chapter 8)
The deterministic safety supervisor running at $1000\text{ Hz}$ on a dedicated bare-metal microcontroller. Grounded in formal **Control Barrier Functions (CBF)** ($h(x) \ge 0$) and dynamic stopping distance envelopes ($d_{\text{stop}} \le d_{\text{clearance}}$), the MCU intercepts all proposed action chunks, computes minimal-intervention quadratic programs, and writes safe motor currents ($u_t$) while executing deterministic emergency fallback chains upon safety vetoes (`ENF-01`).

---

## The Bench Reality on the TinyAgent

Throughout Part II, learners construct and verify the complete closed-loop pipeline on the **Arduino UNO Q Hardware Kit**:

* **DMA Ingestion & Affordance Extraction:** Capturing MIPI-CSI camera frames on the Linux MPU, executing INT8 DINOv2 feature extraction on the NPU, and publishing 3D bounding box coordinates into shared memory.
* **Latent State & TTL Tracking:** Maintaining an $SE(3)$ transform tree while simulating optical camera occlusions, verifying that state confidence decays and triggers safe re-acquisition states.
* **VLM Intent & Leases:** Streaming natural language goals from an edge VLM into an expiring intent register with a $1500\text{ ms}$ validity horizon.
* **Action Chunking & Jerk Smoothing:** Running an ACT diffusion policy unrolling 16-step joint trajectories, measuring joint jerk ($\dddot{q}$) on an oscilloscope to prove temporal ensembling eliminates discontinuous torque spikes.
* **1 kHz MCU Safety Enforcer:** Implementing a real-time Control Barrier Function loop in C++ on the Cortex-M4 MCU that successfully vetoes colliding trajectory proposals and clamps velocity within $2\text{ ms}$.

---

## The Accumulating Design Dossier: Exiting Part II

Upon completing Part II, the engineering team locks five core operational artifacts in the **Cumulative Design Dossier**:

1. `OBS-01` (**Observation Contract**): Defines camera resolutions, DMA buffer addresses, timestamp synchronization protocols, and spatial affordance token formats.
2. `STATE-01` (**State, Frame Tree & Timing Model**): Formulates $SE(3)$ transformation chains, velocity prediction buffers, and state validity time-to-live thresholds ($\text{TTL}_{\text{state}} = 80\text{ ms}$).
3. `INTENT-01` (**Policy Interface & Intent Schema**): Freezes VLM goal representations, 3D workspace boundaries, and intent lease expiration windows ($t_{\text{expire}} = 1500\text{ ms}$).
4. `PLAN-01` (**Planning & Trajectory Schema**): Specifies action chunk horizons ($H=16$), inference frequencies ($30\text{ Hz}$), and maximum derivative limits ($\dot{q}_{\text{max}}, \ddot{q}_{\text{max}}, \dddot{q}_{\text{max}}$).
5. `ENF-01` (**Enforcement Design**): Freezes the $1000\text{ Hz}$ MCU safety enforcer C++ contracts, Control Barrier Function parameters ($\gamma, \alpha$), dynamic stopping envelopes ($d_{\text{stop}}$), and Category 0/1/2 emergency stop state machines.
